claim: A learned Process Reward Model (PRM) giving dense, line-level feedback during code generation, used as both reward and value-function initialization, significantly boosts RL-driven code generation performance especially on long-horizon tasks.
stance_target: novelty of 'dense process supervision beats sparse outcome reward for code RL' as an unclaimed AAAI-viable finding
scope_conditions: RL for code generation, long-horizon complex tasks, Oct 2024 - Feb 2025
quoted_support: We explore various strategies for training PRMs and integrating them into the RL framework, finding that using PRMs both as dense rewards and for value function initialization significantly boosts performance.

claim: Sparse outcome-only reward for code RL yields zero learning signal when generated code fails all unit tests, motivating dense process-level feedback.
stance_target: motivation shared with the per-requirement dense reward pivot direction
scope_conditions: RL with unit test feedback for code generation
quoted_support: When generated code fails all unit tests, no learning signal is received, hindering progress on complex tasks.
